ei.title: Fake or Fact, That Is the Question

fullPassage:
Fake or Fact, That Is the Question

British writer Oobah Butler wanted to experiment with how easily one can manipulate public opinion online. He created a fake restaurant called The Shed at Dulwich. Butler set up an account for his "restaurant" on a popular online review site. He did not provide an exact address and wrote it was reservations only. He did this to make people think The Shed was a special restaurant.

He faked photos of The Shed's food with shaving cream, whitening tablets, and even his own foot. He then asked his friends to write favorable fake reviews on the review site.

Things quickly got, in Butler's words, "a little out of hand." From the lowest of the charts of the review site, The Shed continuously climbed the London rankings. He started getting e-mails and phone calls requesting reservations. Interest further increased when he told callers The Shed was "fully booked for the next six weeks."

Even funnier, food suppliers started guessing The Shed's address and sent him free samples, and many job applications came in. These things happened without Butler serving a single meal. The Shed eventually became London's number-one restaurant on one of the most trusted restaurant review sites. According to Butler, The Shed held that ranking for two weeks.

Butler's story shows that much of what we see on the Internet cannot be trusted. This emphasizes the importance of digital literacy. Digital literacy is about more than just using computers. It is the ability to use digital technology to find, evaluate, create, and communicate information. To become digitally literate, we need to develop an attitude and knowledge that enable us to detect false information online. False information is any information that misinforms or deceives people. It can be about anything such as health, the environment, and economics across many platforms. It can be influential, as The Shed incident shows.

If people had been digitally literate, they would not have been fooled by The Shed experiment so easily. Digitally literate people would have carefully considered information about The Shed without being distracted by other people's reactions. They would have been suspicious that the restaurant did not have an address. They would have wondered why reviews on the restaurant did not appear in other more credible media. If they had done these things, they would likely have suspected that something was not right.

Fortunately, The Shed incident was an experiment that caused little damage. However, false information can cause emotional or financial harm to people. For example, false information about a certain gender or belief group can stir up hatred against that group. It can cause fights between those who support the group and those who do not. In addition, misleading online reviews about questionable products often trick people into wasting money.

To avoid being deceived by false information, we need to develop a habit of critically evaluating what we see online. If you see a story that looks too good or too bad to be true, check the source first. Look at the website the story comes from. Does it look real? Are there spelling errors? Does it have other stories or just the one you read? Check that the story contains references and links to other information. Click on those links and see if the other information looks reliable. Websites with false information often do not have many real stories about other topics. They also often have lots of advertisements that pop up when you visit the sites.

You should then check the credibility of the content creator. If a story has no writer's name, this could be a sign that its content is questionable. If there is a name, find out what and where the person has reported before. If the person has not written anything else or writes for a website that looks unreliable, think twice before believing the content.

Finally, check who else is reporting the story. If no other media are reporting the same story, the story may not be true. Pick a few keywords from the story and put them in a search site to see if other media are supporting the story.

Sorting through the vast amount of information created and shared online is challenging. However, it is important that we know what false information is and how it spreads. The better we recognize false information, the better we will be at avoiding it and helping others do the same.

questions.passage: British writer Oobah Butler wanted to experiment with how easily one can (A)[manipulate / manufacture] public opinion online. He created a fake restaurant called The Shed at Dulwich. Butler set up an account for his "restaurant" on a popular online review site. He did not provide an exact address and wrote it was reservations only. He did this to make people think The Shed was a (B)[special / spatial] restaurant. He faked photos of The Shed's food with shaving cream, whitening tablets, and even his own foot. He then asked his friends to write (C)[favorable / fearful] fake reviews on the review site.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 사람들이 온라인에서 여론을 쉽게 조작할 수 있는지 실험하고 싶었습니다. The Shed가 특별한 레스토랑이라고 생각하게 만들었습니다. 친구들에게 호의적인 가짜 리뷰를 쓰도록 부탁했습니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① manipulate — special — favorable
❌ ② manufacture — special — fearful
❌ ③ manipulate — spatial — fearful
❌ ④ manufacture — spatial — favorable
✅ (A) manipulate: 여론을 '조작하다'. manufacture(제조하다)는 물건 생산에 사용. ✅ (B) special: '특별한' 레스토랑. spatial(공간의)은 발음 유사하나 의미 다름. ✅ (C) favorable: '호의적인' 리뷰. fearful(두려운)은 리뷰 맥락과 불일치.
det.tip: manipulate(조작하다) vs manufacture(제조하다): 접두사 mani-(손)는 같지만 의미가 다름. favorable(호의적인) ↔ unfavorable(비호의적인).

questions.passage: It is the ability to use digital technology to find, evaluate, create, and communicate information. To become digitally literate, we need to develop an attitude and knowledge that enable us to (A)[detect / deflect] false information online. False information is any information that misinforms or (B)[deceives / decides] people. It can be about anything such as health, the environment, and economics across many platforms. It can be (C)[influential / infertile], as The Shed incident shows. If people had been digitally literate, they would not have been fooled by The Shed experiment so easily.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 거짓 정보를 감지할 수 있게 해주는 태도와 지식을 개발해야 합니다. 거짓 정보는 사람들을 잘못 알게 하거나 속이는 정보입니다. The Shed 사건이 보여주듯이 영향력 있을 수 있습니다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① deflect — decides — influential
❌ ② deflect — deceives — infertile
✅ ③ detect — deceives — influential
❌ ④ detect — decides — infertile
✅ (A) detect: 거짓 정보를 '감지하다'. deflect(빗나가게 하다)는 문맥 불일치. ✅ (B) deceives: 사람들을 '속이다'. decides(결정하다)는 형태 유사하나 의미 다름. ✅ (C) influential: '영향력 있는'. infertile(불모의)은 의미 전혀 다름.
det.tip: detect(감지하다) = 숨겨진 것을 찾아내다. deceive(속이다): de-(반대) + ceive(잡다) = 잘못 잡게 하다.

questions.passage: It can be influential, as The Shed incident shows. If people had been digitally literate, they would not have been fooled by The Shed experiment so easily. Digitally literate people would have carefully (A)[considered / consumed] information about The Shed without being distracted by other people's reactions. They would have been (B)[suspicious / supportive] that the restaurant did not have an address. They would have wondered why reviews on the restaurant did not appear in other more (C)[credible / creditable] media. If they had done these things, they would likely have suspected that something was not right.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 디지털 리터러시가 있는 사람들은 다른 사람들의 반응에 흔들리지 않고 정보를 신중하게 고려했을 것입니다. 주소가 없다는 것에 의심했을 것입니다. 더 신뢰할 만한 매체에 왜 리뷰가 나오지 않는지 궁금해했을 것입니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① considered — suspicious — credible
❌ ② consumed — suspicious — creditable
❌ ③ considered — supportive — creditable
❌ ④ consumed — supportive — credible
✅ (A) considered: 정보를 신중하게 '고려하다'. consumed(소비하다)는 정보를 비판적으로 판단하는 맥락과 불일치. ✅ (B) suspicious: 주소 없음에 '의심스러운'. supportive(지지하는)는 정반대. ✅ (C) credible: '신뢰할 만한' 매체. creditable(칭찬할 만한)은 형태 유사하나 의미 다름.
det.tip: credible(신뢰할 만한) vs creditable(칭찬할 만한): 어근 cred-(믿다)는 같지만 접미사가 다름. suspicious: suspect(의심하다)의 형용사형.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: The Shed는 ①계속해서 런던 순위를 올랐습니다. 예약을 ②요청하는 이메일과 전화를 받기 시작했습니다. 완전히 예약됐다고 하자 관심이 더 ③감소했습니다. 음식 공급업체들이 무료 ④샘플을 보냈습니다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①continuously(계속해서): 순위가 계속 올라감 적절. ✅ ②requesting(요청하는): 예약을 요청하는 전화 적절. ❌ ③decreased(감소했다): 원문은 'increased(증가했다)'. 예약이 꽉 찼다고 하면 관심이 더 '증가'하는 것이 맥락에 맞음. ✅ ④samples(샘플): 무료 샘플을 보냄 적절.

questions.passage: Butler's story shows that much of what we see on the Internet cannot be trusted. This emphasizes the importance of digital literacy. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 디지털 기술을 사용하여 정보를 찾고, ①평가하고, 만들고, 전달하는 능력입니다. ②거짓 정보를 감지할 수 있게 해 줍니다. 거짓 정보는 사람들에게 ③알려주는 정보입니다. ④영향력 있을 수 있습니다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①evaluate(평가하다): 정보를 평가하는 것 적절. ✅ ②false(거짓의): 거짓 정보 감지 적절. ❌ ③informs(알려주다): 원문은 'misinforms(잘못 알리다)'. 거짓 정보는 사람들을 '잘못 알리거나' 속이는 것이지 올바르게 '알려주는' 것이 아님. ✅ ④influential(영향력 있는): The Shed 사건처럼 영향력 있음 적절.
det.tip: misinform(잘못 알리다) vs inform(알리다): 접두사 mis-(잘못)가 핵심. misinform ≈ 거짓 정보를 전달하다.

He faked photos of The Shed's food with shaving cream, whitening tablets, and even his own foot. He then asked his friends to write favorable fake reviews on the review site.

Things quickly got, in Butler's words, "a little out of hand." From the lowest of the charts of the review site, The Shed continuously climbed the London rankings. He started getting e-mails and phone calls requesting reservations. Interest further increased when he told callers The Shed was "fully booked for the next six weeks."

Even funnier, food suppliers started guessing The Shed's address and sent him free samples, and many job applications came in. These things happened without Butler serving a single meal. The Shed eventually became London's number-one restaurant on one of the most trusted restaurant review sites. According to Butler, The Shed held that ranking for two weeks.

Butler's story shows that much of what we see on the Internet cannot be trusted. This emphasizes the importance of digital literacy. Digital literacy is about more than just using computers. It is the ability to use digital technology to find, evaluate, create, and communicate information. To become digitally literate, we need to develop an attitude and knowledge that enable us to detect false information online. False information is any information that misinforms or deceives people. It can be about anything such as health, the environment, and economics across many platforms. It can be influential, as The Shed incident shows.

If people had been digitally literate, they would not have been fooled by The Shed experiment so easily. Digitally literate people would have carefully considered information about The Shed without being distracted by other people's reactions. They would have been suspicious that the restaurant did not have an address. They would have wondered why reviews on the restaurant did not appear in other more credible media. If they had done these things, they would likely have suspected that something was not right.

Fortunately, The Shed incident was an experiment that caused little damage. However, false information can cause emotional or financial harm to people. For example, false information about a certain gender or belief group can stir up hatred against that group. It can cause fights between those who support the group and those who do not. In addition, misleading online reviews about questionable products often trick people into wasting money.

To avoid being deceived by false information, we need to develop a habit of critically evaluating what we see online. If you see a story that looks too good or too bad to be true, check the source first. Look at the website the story comes from. Does it look real? Are there spelling errors? Does it have other stories or just the one you read? Check that the story contains references and links to other information. Click on those links and see if the other information looks reliable. Websites with false information often do not have many real stories about other topics. They also often have lots of advertisements that pop up when you visit the sites.

You should then check the credibility of the content creator. If a story has no writer's name, this could be a <u>sign</u> that its content is questionable. If there is a name, find out what and where the person has reported before. If the person has not written anything else or writes for a website that looks unreliable, think twice before believing the content.

Finally, check who else is reporting the story. If no other media are reporting the same story, the story may not be true. Pick a few keywords from the story and put them in a search site to see if other media are supporting the story.

Sorting through the vast amount of information created and shared online is challenging. However, it is important that we know what false information is and how it spreads. The better we recognize false information, the better we will be at avoiding it and helping others do the same.

det.tip: sign의 다의어: (1) 간판/표지판 (2) 신호/징후 (3) 서명하다. 'a sign that ~' = ~라는 징후/신호.

questions.passage: Things quickly got, in Butler's words, "a little out of hand." From the lowest of the charts of the review site, The Shed __________ climbed the London rankings. (continuous)
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) (   ) 쓰시오.

det.korean: The Shed는 계속해서 런던 순위를 올랐습니다.
det.analysis: ✅ continuously: 동사 climbed를 수식하는 부사 필요. continuous(형용사) → continuously(부사). '-ly'를 붙여 부사로 변환.
det.tip: 형용사 → 부사: continuous → continuously. 동사를 수식할 때는 부사를 사용. continuous(계속적인) = 끊임없는.

det.analysis: ✅ information: communicate 뒤에 목적어(명사) 필요. inform(동사) → information(명사). '-ation'을 붙여 명사로 변환.
det.tip: 동사 → 명사: inform → information. -ation은 동사를 명사로 바꾸는 대표적 접미사. communicate information = 정보를 전달하다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 우리가 거짓 정보를 더 잘 알아볼수록, 그것을 피하고 다른 사람들도 그렇게 하도록 돕는 데 더 잘할 것입니다.
det.analysis: ✅ ②recognize(인식하다/알아보다): 거짓 정보를 알아봐야 피할 수 있다는 글의 핵심 메시지. 'the better ~ the better' 비례 구문. ❌ ①spread(퍼뜨리다): 거짓 정보를 퍼뜨리는 것은 글의 메시지와 정반대. ❌ ③create(만들다): 거짓 정보를 만드는 것도 반대. ❌ ④ignore(무시하다): 무시가 아닌 적극적 인식이 필요.
det.tip: recognize(인식하다) = 알아보다, 식별하다. 'The 비교급 ~, the 비교급 ~' = ~할수록 더 ~하다. 글의 마지막 문장 = 핵심 주제.
